lines: Begin on the saved Daily Time Report number two for the fictional
community support deployment.
The report is Draft.
Check the crew, incident reference, resource order, request number, cost
code and point of hire so you are reviewing the intended assignment.
Its notes distinguish personnel travel and coordination from
separately recorded resource time.
This lesson starts with those saved entries and a training expense
already present, then follows submission and independent approval.
In Actions, Save and Save and submit are separate choices.
Select Save and submit and accept its confirmation for this training report.
The returned page shows Saved, the Submitted badge and a submission time.
Approved still has a dash.
Verify that saved state before handing the report to a reviewer.
Submission records that handoff; it does not mean that a different
person has already approved the time.
Notice that Save remains available on this Submitted report.
The header fields are still editable at this stage in the recorded example.
The submission timestamp and the empty Approved value
make the distinction visible.
Review the report’s state and the controls actually offered on your screen instead
of treating submission as a final lock.
The approved-state readback later in this walkthrough will
show the different result.
Scroll to Review while signed in as the submitter, Wallace Boden.
The notice says that you submitted this time report or have hours on it,
so another approver must approve it.
Approve is not offered to this account here.
Follow that separation of duties by having a different authorized
approver review the report.
This is a visible restriction in the local training exercise, not an approval
that was completed by the submitter.
The same report is now open under the separate authorized
Kelly Severide account.
Review the time-entry subjects, entry types, start and end
times, breaks and distance, along with the supporting expense.
This account is offered Approve in Review.
After checking the intended report, select Approve and accept its confirmation.
Use an authorized reviewer who is independent of the submitted
report, rather than changing the report merely to bypass the notice.
The saved result now shows Approved.
Actions lists both the earlier submission time and the later approval time.
The Save and Save and submit buttons are no longer present in that panel.
The report’s reference fields are greyed out.
Check these visible results after approval so the report’s state agrees
with the action you intended to take.
A timestamped approved report is a different result from
an unsaved review screen.
Scroll through the approved report.
The existing entry controls are disabled and Add entry is no longer offered.
Under Expenses, the saved Fuel row still contains the training receipt description,
twenty-four dollars and fifty cents in U S currency, and its attachment icon.
The expense-entry form is no longer shown here.
The signature fields remain blank.
This exercise verifies approval and retained supporting detail; it does not
create a contractor or customer signature.
Use Back to deployment and review the report row in the Time reports section.
Status is Approved.
Submitted names Wallace Boden with the submission time, and Approved names Kelly
Severide with the later approval time.
This index provides a second readback of the separate users.
Invoice is blank in this operational-only exercise.
Report approval does not, by itself, establish that an invoice, payment
or payroll action has occurred.
Use this process wherever your department needs a checked deployment time record.
Wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams can review
crew duty and resource time.
Search-and-rescue, security, community paramedicine and mental health teams can
review appropriate deployment activity, as can fire and E M S organizations.
Confirm the assignment, submit the report, have a different permitted
reviewer approve it, and verify the saved state and supporting detail.
Keep that time-report approval separate from the deployment’s own status.
